title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.78). X is a space stratified by a poset I. X_i^* are the strata, X_i = ⊔_{j≤i} X_j^* is the closed set they generate, and V_{i_0…i_n} (i_0<…<i_n) are pro-tubular neighbourhoods and their iterated intersections. X is recovered by gluing: X ≅ colim over flags of V_{i_0…i_n}, or equivalently colim of (V_i, V_ij). For a 'tranche' or 'bande' J ⊂ I (a convex subset), X_J^* = ⊔_{i∈J} X_i^* is locally closed. It inherits a J-stratification with relative neighbourhoods V^J = V ∩ X_J^*, and it is again the colimit of its V^J (formula 61 on p.78).

This page.
(1) Take two bands J ⊂ J'. Then X_J^* ⊂ X_{J'}^* is a closed union of strata inside X_{J'}^*. Its pro-tubular neighbourhood there is described by the same gluing recipe, using only indices in J but neighbourhoods relative to J' (formula 62): V(X_J^*, X_{J'}^*) = colim_{i,j∈J}(V_i^{J'}, V_ij^{J'}). For comparison, X_J^* = colim_{i,j∈J}(V_i^J, V_ij^J).
(2) NB, a reduction step. By deleting the ideal J̃'∖J' (whose strata form a closed set), one may assume J' = I and J an ideal of I. More symmetrically, the configuration is J_0 ⊂ J_1 ⊂ J_2, three ideals, with J = J_1∖J_0 and J' = J_2∖J_0.
(3) For K ⊂ I, define the 'deleted' neighbourhood V^{J'}_{J,K} = V(X_J^*, X_{J'}^*) ∖ (X_K ∩ V(X_J^*, X_{J'}^*)). This is the tubular neighbourhood with the closed union of strata X_K removed, i.e. a generalized punctured neighbourhood or link.
(4) Observation (63): for k ∈ I, V_J^{J'} ∩ X_k = ∅ ⇔ X_J^* ∩ X_k = ∅ ⇔ (i ≤ k ⇒ i ∉ J). The reason is that X_k = ⊔_{i≤k} X_i^*, and a neighbourhood of X_i^* only meets strata X_j^* with j ≥ i.

Purpose. These are preparations for the next page. There Grothendieck introduces V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^* for two bands, the 'prolongements de recollement', and the domination relation J ≺ L on bands. The aim is a combinatorial calculus of neighbourhoods and links indexed by convex subposets, towards the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space into gluing data.
errors: No real error. (63) must be read at the level of germs or pro-neighbourhoods: the forward implication V∩X_k=∅ ⇒ X_J^*∩X_k=∅ is trivial. The converse needs that a neighbourhood of X_i^* meets only strata X_j^* with j ≥ i, which holds for pro-neighbourhoods but not for an arbitrary fixed neighbourhood.

Notation is unstable on this page and its neighbours: V(X_J^*,X_{J'}^*), V_J^{J'} and later V_J^L are used for related but distinct objects. Formula numbers (62), (63) are reused on the next page with different meanings.

ideas.what: Pro-tubular neighbourhood of a union of strata indexed by a convex subposet (band) J inside the space of strata indexed by a larger band J', expressed as a colimit of the relative basic neighbourhoods over J
ideas.modern_name: Neighbourhoods and links of locally closed unions of strata; restriction of stratified spaces to convex subposets (Quinn homotopy links, Lurie HA A.6, Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988), Hughes; Lurie (Higher Algebra, A.6); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017); Haine (2018+)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched (Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, tame topology and 'déploiement'); these details are unpublished

ideas.what: Reduction of a pair of bands J⊂J' to a chain of three ideals J_0⊂J_1⊂J_2 by discarding a closed union of strata
ideas.modern_name: Locally closed / convex subposets as differences of down-sets

ideas.what: Deleted neighbourhoods V∖X_K, and the criterion V_J∩X_k=∅ ⇔ no i≤k in J
ideas.modern_name: Generalized (multi-step) links of strata; deleted tubular neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn; Lurie; Douteau–Waas (stratified links indexed by flags)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a calculus of tubular neighbourhoods and deleted neighbourhoods indexed by pairs of convex subposets (bands) J⊂J' and subsets K. On the next page this becomes gluing maps V_J^L and a domination relation J≺L on bands. It is an early, purely topological attempt at describing a stratified space by link data indexed by convex subposets, close in spirit to later ∞-categorical exit-path/link descriptions. On this page it is only set-up, not a finished result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme (1981–82) already worked with links indexed by convex subposets, prefiguring the unzipping and link formalisms of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka and Haine. No new theorem is visible on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping in an unpublished programme: relative pro-tubular neighbourhoods for bands of strata and an easy disjointness criterion. Historically interesting as a precursor of modern link/unzipping formalisms, but nothing here goes beyond what is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'deux b. [?]' is 'deux bandes J ⊂ J′', matching the use of 'bande' on the next page.
Line 3: read 'en regardant les pro-voisinages tubulaires' ('pro' inserted above 'voisinages'; a crossed-out word follows).
(62): the image shows lim_{i,j∈J}(V_i^{J'}, V_{ij}^{J'}) with double index ij, not V_j^{J'}. The boxed parenthetical likewise reads X_J^* = lim_{i,j∈J}(V_i^J, V_{ij}^J).

NB: 'J_0^* = J̃∖J' is better read 'J_0′ = J̃′∖J′' or similar (the ideal removed). The following line reads roughly '(on est ramené au cas où on a dans I J_0 ⊂ J_1 ⊂ J_2 trois idéaux, et J = J_1∖J_0, J′ = J_2∖J_0 …)'.
(63): the image reads 'V^{J'}_{J,k} def= V_J^{J'} ∩ X_k = ∅ ⟺ X_J^* ∩ X_k = ∅'. The struck line below reads '⟺ ∀ i∈I, i≤k ⇒ i∉J'.
Left margin (rotated) begins roughly 'On a V^{J'}_J … (62)' and 'On a V_J^{J'} = Ṽ_J^{J_0}' (approximate). It then states a condition that X_J^* be … in X_{J'}^*, i.e. an ideal; partly illegible.
The page carries two large diagonal strokes, indicating Grothendieck crossed out (superseded) the whole page; the next page restarts the construction.
